content.text: All responsive provisions are located and consistent; no other change-of-control or assignment mechanic exists.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or to an M&A/asset-sale successor without Vendor's consent (Affiliate is broadly defined at 1.1 by >50% control or power to direct management); 24.2 bars Vendor from assigning, delegating material performance, or transferring by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, subject only to a reasonableness standard, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard to other assignments; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control. Section 13.3 reinforces our licence-transfer right on a permitted assignment. Only minor sub-elements fall short of ideal wording — the competitor bar is framed as "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute, and the reasonableness qualifier in 24.2 is keyed to an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing — which we note but do not redline given consent is required for every Vendor assignment in any event. No walk-away features (no blanket bar on Customer assignment, no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right) are present.
